changes: FIX THE paths: SCOPE (load-bearing bug, council-confirmed). `**/.claude/**`+`**/.agents/**` (copied verbatim from fan-out-contract.md:2-4) means the rule never loads for ordinary project/research sessions — deployed-but-inert for most tasks per the loader semantics in lint-rules-loading.ps1:41-47 — and injects MID-TASK when a session merely touches a harness file (observed live this session: rule bodies injected on Read/Glob of the rules dir), violating the rule's own 'proposal before execution, never mid-task' clause. A rule meant to govern ALL non-trivial tasks has no valid path scope: either land it as an AGENTS-RUNTIME §1 amendment (always-on, with a thin-docs offset) or scope it to the artifact classes it actually protects. Also state how it composes with the metaswarm gates already mandatory at HOME cwd (C:\Users\Prekzursil\CLAUDE.md 'Workflow Enforcement': design gate, plan gate, execution-method ask) so it does not become a sixth stacked ceremony.

STRIKE THE PRECEDENCE GRAB. 'It replaces those artifacts [§1 goal-restate + §1b assumption ledger]' — a rules/common file cannot amend the layer-3 contract (AGENTS-RUNTIME §10 precedence: contract > project governance > skills/rules). Reword as 'the proposal SATISFIES §1/§1b for the covered task', or amend AGENTS-RUNTIME §1/§1b directly so the two artifacts stop contradicting each other in every session that loads both.

DE-BLOCK UNATTENDED EXECUTION. 'Wide or irreversible scope ⇒ blocking approval gate' must degrade to propose-and-log when no human is in the loop (Workflow fan-outs, codex-fleet nightly sweeps, cron, subagents) — parallel() has no per-agent timeout, so a honored block deadlocks the phase, and a bypassed block is pure paid ceremony. Explicitly exempt delegated units: the ORCHESTRATOR owns the one proposal; workers never re-propose (fan-out-contract.md A1: compliance comes from the spawn prompt, nothing is inherited).

DEFINE 'non-trivial' MECHANICALLY and settle the loop question. Give a threshold (e.g. ≥3 files or ≥2 dependent phases, mirroring the /start-task 3+-file rule) and state that an N-iteration fix/review loop is ONE task with ONE proposal, REPLAN covering pivots — otherwise ceremony volume is agent-choice and multiplies ×N.

RECONCILE WITH ALWAYS-PUSH. State that the gate fires BEFORE the first commit and that post-commit state is pushed and effectively irreversible (scripts/git-hooks/post-commit-autopush pushes every commit immediately, fail-open); never delay a push to wait for approval, and never park work on a 'proposal branch' awaiting review (strands exactly what ALWAYS-PUSH exists to protect).

REGISTER THE REPLAN LOOPS. gap_check.py:48 reads ONLY OPEN-LOOPS.md (+ git state, 2.5s budget) — proposal/REPLAN artifacts are invisible to it. Either declare proposals session-scoped TASKBOX items (in-flight work) or explicitly outside §1c; do NOT let replans be silently untracked (violates 'nothing left abandoned') nor dumped as L-rows into OPEN-LOOPS (turns the silent-when-clean Stop hook into per-turn noise — the tuned-out-gate failure its own docstring warns against).

FIX THE VERIFIED-WRONG CITATION. arXiv 2402.05120 is 'More Agents Is All You Need' (sampling-and-voting ensembles), NOT judge panels — confirmed by primary fetch today; it cannot support 'judge-panel is the exception that scales with agent count'. Recite or delete that line, and re-verify the remaining four citations (2503.13657, 2305.18323, 2312.04511, the Anthropic 15x post) before install: a false premise installed into loaded rules propagates into every session's reasoning (measured estate precedent: 42% of audit findings refuted at 89% self-rated confidence, 2026-07-13).

KILL THE ANTI-FAN-OUT DEFAULT FRAMING. 'Single-agent loop is the DEFAULT topology; tree/DAG/panel must earn their ~15x cost' inverts the owner's standing preferences — parallel-by-default for independent work, 50-100-agent fan-outs, 'quality over cost — usage is not a constraint' (performance.md; feedback_desired_agent_character; never-self-throttle). Make BUDGET a reporting field, not a justification tax on concurrency.

CAP THE CEREMONY AND PAY THE TOKEN DEBT. Hard-cap the proposal (≤150 words / 6 fields, ReWOO-reference style), state the rule's own context cost (~1K tokens per triggered session + the §12 row lands in the ALWAYS-ON contract), and offset it against the open 'thin-docs diet' loop — context-reduction.md §8: ~14.7K always-on tokens is ALREADY a flagged violation and 'a new rule must replace bulk, not add'. Net-zero or negative always-on bytes, demonstrated before the lint passes.

LAND IT THROUGH THE PROVEN INSTALL PATH (precedent: fork-lifecycle.md for the same-day 2026-09-30 fork directive). Add the AGENTS-RUNTIME §12 table row; run scripts/sync-rules.ps1; assert scripts/lint-rules-loading.ps1 exits 0 (cited + deployed + loadable — the exact trio whose absence made every authored rule inert before 2026-09-25); record the DIRECTIVES.md row with WHERE it is enforced and the EVIDENCE (per §1d, a directive is done when a mechanism proves it works, not when a file exists); commit AND push (ALWAYS-PUSH). WORST REALISTIC CASE (composite, anchored to disk evidence; each branch graded separately).

T-0, 03:00 — the nightly codex-fleet sweep launches across the 26-repo fleet. Its orchestrator session reads a script under ~/.agents to build spawn prompts; the path-triggered loader injects the rule MID-SESSION (mechanics demonstrated live in this red-team session: rule bodies injected the moment the rules dir was touched — including rules the task never asked for). The rule is now live for a run that started under a different regime, violating its own clause "Proposal happens BEFORE execution, never mid-task" — the loader, not the agent, breaks it. [almost certain 0.90-0.95 — loader semantics per lint-rules-loading.ps1:41-47 ("the loader keys off a paths: list in the frontmatter") + observed injection behavior]

T+2min — per fan-out-contract.md A1 ("nothing is inherited from the global contract... Zero inheritance from AGENTS.md §7 was measured"), the orchestrator knows compliance requires inlining, so it threads the 6-field proposal requirement into all 60 spawn prompts: ~24K tokens of proposal ceremony across the wave, none of which any human will read before the units act. [arithmetic certain; adoption shape likely 0.55-0.80]

T+10min — each unit classifies its work "wide" (multi-file by design; on this estate wide is the NORM — fleet sweeps, harness edits, multi-disk estates), triggering "Wide or irreversible scope ⇒ blocking approval gate." No human is awake. Branch A: compliant units stop and wait → parallel()/Workflow has NO per-agent timeout (measured: one hung agent deadlocks the phase; detect = write-freeze >25min) → the sweep burns its quota window producing zero PRs; the failure is discovered at 09:00 as "flake." Branch B: units self-authorize under propose-and-proceed → the ceremony tokens were spent, zero steering occurred, and the gate that was supposed to add human oversight added only latency. Either branch is a pure disbenefit; the rule cannot win unattended. [likely 0.55-0.80 — depends on model compliance interpretation; the deadlock shape is precedented by cross-vendor-dispatch.md's hang catalogue]

T+40min — the units that proceeded start committing. post-commit-autopush (on disk: ~/.agents/scripts/git-hooks/post-commit-autopush; fail-open, pushes every commit immediately) fires per commit. The owner's 09:00 steer now lands on refs already pushed — "steering while steering is still cheap" was architecturally illusory: the rule installs a checkpoint that ALWAYS-PUSH removes. Worse, REPLAN triggers fired 14 times across units; the rule assigns them NO register. gap_check.py reads ONLY OPEN-LOOPS.md rows + git state (gap_check.py:48, BUDGET_S=2.5) — so the replans are either invisible (silent abandonment, the exact §1c violation the hook exists to catch) or get dumped as L-rows into OPEN-LOOPS, where they expire and turn a "SILENT WHEN CLEAN" hook into per-turn noise — and "a gate that is tuned out is worse than no gate" (gap_check.py:15-16, the owner's own constraint: "no downsides while also not being noise"). A REAL expired loop gets missed in the noise. [almost certain 0.90-0.95 that one of the two branches occurs; which one depends on agent behavior]

09:10 — the owner's interactive session at HOME touches a harness file; the rule injects, stacking a SIXTH pre-execution ceremony on top of clarify-first (§1), assumption ledger (§1b), tiered asks (§1c), and the metaswarm gates already mandatory at this cwd (C:\Users\Prekzursil\CLAUDE.md "Workflow Enforcement": Design Review Gate 5 agents + Plan Review Gate 3 reviewers + ALWAYS-ask execution method). Context is already ~14.7K always-on tokens OVER the estate's own budget (context-reduction.md §8, open "thin-docs diet" loop — "a new rule must replace bulk, not add"); the rule's ~1K tokens per triggered session plus its §12 contract row push autocompaction earlier — a named quality harm, i.e. decreased harness efficiency, on the mandate's exact axis. Meanwhile the rule's precedence grab ("it REPLACES §1/§1b artifacts") contradicts the always-loaded layer-3 contract (§10: a rules/common file sits BELOW project governance), so fresh sessions see two authorities claiming the same slot and behave nondeterministically; and its "single-agent loop is the DEFAULT topology / fan-out must earn its 15x" framing inverts the owner's standing parallel-by-default, quality-over-cost preferences (performance.md: "usage is not a constraint"). [always-on regression: almost certain 0.90-0.95; behavioral drift: likely 0.55-0.80]

The sting: the one hard factual line the rule installed — "Judge-panel is the exception that scales with agent count (arXiv 2402.05120)" — is FALSE as cited. Primary fetch today: 2402.05120 is "More Agents Is All You Need," a sampling-and-voting paper; "judge panels"/"agents-as-judges" appear nowhere in it. Every session that loads the rule now reasons from a fabricated premise — the estate's measured failure class (2026-07-13 audit: 42% of 225 findings REFUTED at 89% self-rated confidence). [confirmed by primary source]

Net disbenefit ledger as drafted: false governance (rule inert for every non-.claude/.agents task — the council's confirmed scope bug; identical globs exist at fan-out-contract.md:2-4), ~1K tokens/trigger + always-on growth against a measured budget violation, deadlock-or-bypass in every unattended run, an approval checkpoint autopush makes unreachable, gap-check noise or silent replan abandonment, a sixth interactive ceremony the owner already routes around (`*` bypass, /start-task carve-outs), contract-level contradiction, preference inversion, and one verified-wrong citation. NONE of these are irreducible — every one is a design defect with a known fix, which is why the ruling is SHIP-WITH-CHANGES and not KILL: the 2026-09-30 owner directive is real, its evidence base is sound in substance, and the estate has a same-day-directive install precedent that satisfies §1d ("a directive records WHERE it is enforced and the EVIDENCE").
